newsitem.title: USA: Conrail, CSX say would meet Norfolk Southern.
newsitem.headline: Conrail, CSX say would meet Norfolk Southern.

text.p: The heads of Conrail Inc and CSX Corp said in a letter to Norfolk Southern Corp Chairman David Goode they would be willing to meet and talk to Goode with an aim toward assuring "strong, viable competition" in the railroad sector.

The letter, sent in response to a letter from Goode on Tuesday calling for talks, said the Conrail and CSX remained "fully committed" to their merger and that a meeting should not be interpreted as a change in position by either side.
A copy of the CSX-Conrail letter was released to Reuters.

A meeting of the three sides would be the first in the course of the three-month takeover battle for Conrail, in which Norfolk Southern is seeking to break up the proposed CSX-Conrail merger and acquire Conrail for itself.

A Norfolk Southern spokesman called the response a "positive development." He said Goode, Conrail Chairman David LeVan and CSX Chairman John Snow had spoken briefly by telephone late Wednesday afternoon but no date had been set for a meeting.
"We appreciate their prompt response and we regard it as a positive development," said Norfolk Southern spokesman Bob Fort.

In their letter, Conrail and CSX said told Goode: "We are fully committed to the CSX/Conrail merger. We believe our merger, together with your participation, will enable us to best serve the interests of all our constituencies, preserve our merger synergies and yield a pro-competitive result."

"We recognize that you have a different view of our merger; nevertheless we should...meet and talk. This can and should be done without any preconditions that would limit our discussions or otherwise prejudice our respective positions," they said.

"Let us be very clear, no one should interpret from our meeting that either party has changed its position. Our objective, which we are sure you share, is to assure that the public's interest in strong, viable competition is met. We want no winner or loser, other than to be sure that the public is a winner," the CSX and Conrail letter said.
The two chairmen said they looked forward to meeting Goode at "his earliest possible convenience."

Goode said in his letter Tuesday that Norfolk Southern would enter talks with a precondition of "recognition" that it had pledged to Conrail shareholders that it would only enter into an agreement with Conrail and CSX that gave Conrail shareholders an all-cash offer of $115 per share, the amount of Norfolk Southern's bid.
